findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded directly in the Lambda function's environment variables in source-controlled Terraform. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Terraform state, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve them and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key, meaning any caller with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can read the decrypted values without a separate KMS grant.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network boundary controlling egress, which aids data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
